title: Vendor availability admission rejection
summary: Implemented a focused admission/scoring slice: low-value third-party channel availability PRs for another provider's model no longer occupy `main_items`; they are audited with `main_reject_reason:"low_value_vendor_availability_pr"` before authoring or repair can make them look more important.

validation_commands: node --test --test-name-pattern "report:draft rejects low-value vendor availability PRs from main admission" tests/unit.test.js
node --test --test-name-pattern "admission scoring|Fable/Mythos|unified candidate roles|rejection reason counts" tests/unit.test.js

lessons.lesson: Admission should reject low-value channel availability PRs explicitly, not rely on prose quality or score ordering.
lessons.evidence: The focused red test failed because an AWS Bedrock-style Claude availability PR still entered `main_items`; after the fix the candidate is absent from `main_items` and records `low_value_vendor_availability_pr`.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep adding admission fixtures for low-value but structurally complete candidates before broad authoring changes.

lessons.lesson: This is still a narrow slice, not a complete admission rewrite.
lessons.evidence: The change only covers third-party model channel availability announcements and does not alter discovery, source lanes, authoring, rendering, or automation.
lessons.recommended_action: Next admission work should add fixtures for vendor partnership PRs, generic availability copy, and high-value official model/provider releases from real dated drafts.

suggestions.issue: Vendor availability announcements could occupy main-story slots because they looked official and structurally complete.
suggestions.evidence: The new test fixture uses an AWS Bedrock-style Claude availability PR; the candidate now receives `main_reject_reason:"low_value_vendor_availability_pr"`.
suggestions.suggestion: Reject low-value third-party model channel availability PRs at admission time and keep them out of `main_items`.
suggestions.expected_benefit: Better first-pass selection: authoring no longer spends effort making low-value channel PRs sound like main stories.
suggestions.promotion_path: Implemented in `src/draft.js`, unit tests, feedback ledger, quick reference, requirements reconciliation, and roadmap evidence text.
validation_evidence: node --test --test-name-pattern "report:draft rejects low-value vendor availability PRs from main admission" tests/unit.test.js

followups.action: Run a real dated draft and inspect whether remaining low-signal vendor/platform items are excluded, merged into original stories, or demoted to signal sections.
Continue admission/scoring with fixtures for generic vendor partnerships and source-health-aware selection before starting broad LLM authoring work.
